description: Caliper saturation refinement sweep on 5-orderer Raft, fresh network per seed. Bracketed between η rate-500 (sustained 468 TPS, 50 ms avg lat) and β rate-1000 (453 TPS with 45% commit timeouts). Identifies sustained throughput plateau and the rate above which queue backlog dominates latency.

key_findings.saturation_plateau_TPS: 503-537 across rate-600 to rate-900 (≈ 7% variation despite 50% increase in send rate) - clear throughput ceiling
key_findings.no_commit_failures: All 270K transactions across 3 seeds × 4 rates committed successfully (0 fails)
key_findings.queue_backlog_dominates_latency: Latency grows nearly linearly: 5.7s (rate-600) → 17.0s (rate-900) as queue accumulates
key_findings.max_latency_far_exceeds_avg: Max latency in seed 1: rate-900 reaches 23.76 s (max) vs 16.81 s (avg)
key_findings.saturation_point_identified: Throughput ceiling on this hardware envelope: ~530 TPS sustained. Anything above creates client-side queue without raising actual blockchain throughput.
key_findings.consistency_across_seeds: TPS std across 3 fresh-bootstrap seeds: 1.31 to 16.80 (mostly within 3%)

comparison_to_other_phases.vs_eta_rate-500: η sustained 468 TPS clean → δ rate-600 sustains 503 TPS, +7.4%
comparison_to_other_phases.vs_beta_rate-1000: β rate-1000 had 453 TPS with 45% timeouts → δ shows queue dominates BEFORE failures
comparison_to_other_phases.interpretation: The β commit timeouts at rate-1000 are an artifact of Caliper's default 7s commit timeout being exceeded once latency grows past it. The actual blockchain CAN commit them (as δ shows), they just exceed the SDK observer window.

related_phases.mu: 5node_extended_conc_2026-06-08 (contrasts SDK 530 TPS ceiling vs native CLI 45 TPS ceiling)
